newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO KEROSENE SUBDUED, NAPHTHA WEAKER WITH CRUDES.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO KEROSENE SUBDUED, NAPHTHA WEAKER WITH CRUDES.

text.p: Kerosene activity remained subdued in afternoon Tokyo trading on Monday on the back of persistently high domestic stocks, while naphtha levels fell due to last Friday's sharp crude oil loss, traders said.
"Most oil firms are unlikely to start importing kerosene for the winter until maybe mid-October," one trader said.
Kerosene stocks at end-June, the latest month for which data is available, were up 28 percent from a year earlier.
Open-spec naphtha was quoted at $205.00/$206.00 per tonne for second-half October delivery. It was said to have been traded at $207.00 on Friday.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), which is mainly used as fuel at thermal power plants, was notionally firmer with a heatwave in Japan setting a bullish tone in the market.
Temperatures in Tokyo have been above average for the past three days.
